issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: Add an overload of the StackTrace constructor to take in an array of frames
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @tommcdon See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Background and motivation StackTrace already contains a constructor that accepts a single frame, accepting multiple frames would seem a logical continuation and allows for nice resolution of stack frames captured from an existing StackTrace object. Because `ToString(TraceFormat traceFormat, StringBuilder sb)` uses `_numOfFrames` rather than the virtual `FrameCount` when calling `GetFrame(int)`, it's unreliable (minus setting the field via reflection) to call `ToString()` on a class derived from `StackTrace` that would allow the specification of a specific set of frames (rather than one frame). ### API Proposal ```csharp namespace System.Diagnostics; public partial class StackTrace { //Additional constructor public StackTrace(StackFrame[] frames) { _stackFrames = frames; _numOfFrames = frames.Length; } } ``` ### API Usage ```csharp // Get a real stack trace var realTrace = new StackTrace(true) // Filter out frames that aren't of interest (things that could identify a customer, generated code, etc.) var filteredFrames = FilterToDesiredFrames(realTrace.GetFrames()); // Construct a fake trace containing the desired frames var fakeTrace = new StackTrace(filteredFrames); // Using the prettification StackTrace applies to its frames Console.WriteLine(fakeTrace); ``` ### Alternative Designs _No response_ ### Risks _No response_
